teaching.hint: What does reverse digit order let you compute immediately at the two list heads?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Because the least-significant digits come first, the lists are already ordered exactly as elementary addition processes columns.
solution_outline.approach: Walk both lists together while either has a node or a carry remains. At each position, add the available digits and carry, append the result digit, and propagate the next carry. A dummy result head keeps every append uniform.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before each step, the output contains the correct digit for every processed position, and the carry is exactly the carry entering the next position.
solution_outline.correctness: The next output digit and carry are the quotient and remainder of the two available digits plus the incoming carry. This preserves the invariant one column at a time. Once both inputs and the carry are exhausted, every position of the sum has been emitted.
solution_outline.complexity: O(max(m, n)) time and O(max(m, n)) output space, with O(1) auxiliary space excluding the returned list.
solution_outline.pitfall: Stopping when the shorter list ends, or when both lists end but a final carry remains, loses required digits.

common_wrong_turns: Converting the entire lists to fixed-width integers
source_fidelity_notes: The decorative source image and repetitive examples were omitted; reverse order, digit bounds, nonempty inputs, and length asymmetry were retained.
